is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles gambiae (s.l.), An. funestus, and An. mascarensis.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F/S (kdr) and Ace-1 G119S (ace-1R) mutations (page 6, 10, 11).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 4 provides the number of mosquitoes genotyped for species identification (n=986) and mentions that 248 were genotyped for G119S (page 10, 11).

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses field-collected mosquitoes from Madagascar (page 3, 4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field data.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides data at the district and commune/village level (Table 1, page 4).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study covers collection periods 2013/2014 and 2015/2016 (Table 1, page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study reports new, original data collected between 2013 and 2016.

supplement.evidence: The necessary data is provided within the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study assessed insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae (s.l.), An. funestus, and An. mascarensis in Madagascar using WHO and CDC bioassays and molecular analysis for kdr and ace-1R mutations. Results showed phenotypic resistance to DDT and pyrethroids in An. gambiae (s.l.) but no detectable kdr or ace-1R mutations, suggesting metabolic resistance mechanisms.
